example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, open bills from Ashford Seating, September. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

chosen.warehouse-receipts-september.xlsx: the name of the user's own receipt sheet

messages.text: Can you check September's supplier bills before we pay them?
Yes. Before I read anything, I need six answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the documents?
How much difference do you accept on price, on quantity and on the total?
Who may approve a purchase order, and up to what amount?
Do you buy services on purchase orders? What replaces a delivery record for them?
Do you have orders or bills in a foreign currency? Which exchange rate do you use?

messages.text: Use MosoFin. We have no tolerance policy. A director approves any order over $2,500. Goods only, all in US dollars. AP owns the exceptions.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and what your books hold
rows: QuickBooks Online Plus, confirmed by name
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

messages.text: Your books hold the bills, the purchase orders and their approvals. They do not hold the goods receipts. Without receipts, I can only do a **two-way match**, and tests 4, 7, 8 and 15 cannot run. Can you attach your delivery records?
Our warehouse keeps them in a spreadsheet. Here it is.

Here is my plan. I match **September's open bills** for **Northbrook Trading** against their purchase orders and your receipts. I use **exact match**, because you gave no tolerance. Your approval matrix applies. This is a **three-way match**. Shall I start?

messages.label: Read the books in one batch
rows: Includes the Ashford Seating bill on PO-1041
messages.summary: 3 reads in one batch, and your sheet. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: All fifteen tests ran, because your sheet records what arrived and its condition. The bill from **Ashford Seating** on **PO-1041** does not agree with the order or the delivery:
messages.after: The headers agree: PO reference, supplier, currency, company and payment terms. A director approved the order. The problems are on the line.

messages.text: That line has three High exceptions. Ashford charged **$1.50 a chair** over the order. Ashford also billed the full 100 chairs, but the warehouse rejected 4 as damaged.

card.title: What you owe on this bill
rows: − 4 damaged chairs billed in full, 4 × $42.00 (exceptions 4 and 15)

messages.after: My recommendation is **Hold**. The line is outside your tolerance, so the matched amount is $0 and the disputed amount is the full $4,350. AP owns all three exceptions.

messages.text: Your sheet also shows three deliveries with a signed receipt and no bill. I checked every bill on their orders, open or paid. None of them bills these goods.
messages.after: AP has nothing to pay here yet. But you owe for these goods, so your accountant must accrue **$3,500** at 30 September.

messages.text: I propose two actions. Each one points to its evidence:

card.title: Proposed actions
head: Action
Amount
Evidence
rows: Ask Ashford for a credit note on PO-1041
PO-1041 price and the signed receipt
Draft accrual at 30 Sep: debit Inventory, credit Accrued Liabilities, GRNI

messages.after: The credit note brings the bill to $4,032. The accrual reverses on 1 October. A person sends the request and posts the entry. I do not pay, hold or post anything.

messages.text: Your report says which match I ran. It has the summary, every line with its match basis, the exceptions with their owners, the month's findings and the coverage.
messages.after: Do you want the report as an Excel file? And do you want me to save your settings for next month?

messages.text: Done. The Excel file has the six sheets. I saved which documents your books hold, the exact-match policy, your approval matrix and the exception owner. Next month, the run starts from them.
